key_terms.meaning:
Markup written in angle brackets, like

or

, that marks where an element starts and ends.

The whole unit: start tag, content, end tag — for example

Hello

.
A name=value pair written inside a start tag that tunes the element, like href="page.html".
Attributes usable on almost any element: id, class, style, title, lang, hidden, data-*.
Elements with no content and no end tag, such as br, img, input, hr, meta, link.
Text between <!-- and --> that the browser ignores but keeps in the source.
An <a href="..."> element that loads another page, a file, an email address or a place inside the page.
The alt attribute of an image, shown when the image fails and read out by screen readers.
The name attribute of an input; it becomes the key in the name=value pair the browser sends.
GET puts the pairs in the URL query string; POST puts them in the request body.
An HTML5 tag that names the role of a region, such as header, nav, main, article, aside, footer.
An inline frame that embeds one whole document, such as a map, inside the current page.
The part of a CSS rule before the braces that says which elements the declarations apply to.
The braces-and-declarations part of a rule, like {color: red; margin: 8px;}.
A weight computed from the selector (inline > id > class/attribute > element) used to break cascade ties.
Every element is a content box plus padding, border and margin; all four widths add to the space used.
A CSS condition, like @media (max-width: 600px), that applies rules only at some screen sizes.
A box with display: flex whose direct children become flex items laid along a main axis.
A row of 12 equal columns; col-4 takes four of twelve, and columns wrap on small screens.
A single-purpose class such as mt-3 or text-center that sets one property, used instead of new CSS.

takeaways: An HTML document is a tree: the html element holds head and body, and every other element hangs inside one of them.
Tags mark boundaries, elements are the whole unit, attributes tune the element, and void elements have no closing tag.
Headings, links, lists, tables and images carry almost all the text and data an ordinary page shows, so write them with meaning.
A form control contributes one name=value pair, and the form's method decides whether those pairs travel in the URL or in the body.
HTML5 semantic elements describe the page's regions, and video, audio and iframe embed other media natively.
A CSS rule is a selector plus a declaration block; when rules clash, the cascade, then specificity, then source order decide.
The box model means the visible size of an element is content + padding + border, with margin pushing neighbours away.
Flexbox arranges items in one direction, Grid in two, and media queries plus the viewport meta tag let one layout serve every screen.
Bootstrap replaces hand-written layout CSS with a 12-column grid, ready components and single-property utility classes.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask you to write real markup or CSS and then justify the choice — a full form, a box-model calculation, a Flexbox or Bootstrap layout, and a reasoned comparison of two techniques.

bank.q: Draw and explain the structure of a minimal HTML5 document, naming the purpose of the doctype, head, title, meta charset and body.
outline: Doctype is not an element; it tells the browser to use standards mode
html is the root; lang attribute declares the language
head holds metadata: charset, title, viewport, linked CSS — nothing visible
body holds visible content
Elements are nested: the document is a tree, indentation shows the levels

bank.q: Distinguish between a tag, an element and an attribute, and explain global attributes and void elements with two examples each.
outline: Tag = the angle-bracket marker; element = start tag + content + end tag
Attribute = name=value inside the start tag; several allowed, order free, values quoted
Global attributes: id, class, style, title, lang, hidden, data-*
Void elements: br, hr, img, input, meta, link — no content, no end tag
Example: has three attributes and is void

bank.q: Explain the CSS box model with a diagram. Given content width 300 px, padding 10 px each side, border 2 px each side and margin 15 px each side, compute the visible width and the total horizontal space occupied.
outline: Four layers: content, padding, border, margin, from inside out
Padding and border add to the visible box; margin is outside
Visible width = 300 + 2×10 + 2×2 = 324 px
Total horizontal space = 324 + 2×15 = 354 px
box-sizing: border-box moves padding and border inside the stated width

bank.q: Write the general syntax of a CSS rule and compare inline, internal and external stylesheets with their precedence and reusability.
outline: Rule = selector + declaration block of property: value pairs
Inline via style attribute — affects one element, highest priority
Internal via <style> in head — one document only
External via <link rel="stylesheet" href="..."> — cached, reused across pages
Order of precedence: inline, then author stylesheet by specificity, then source order

bank.q: List the main HTML5 semantic elements and explain the advantage of semantic markup over div-soup.
outline: header, nav, main, section, article, aside, footer, figure, figcaption
One main per page; article is self-contained, section is a themed block
Readability of source for the team
Accessibility: screen readers and keyboard users get landmarks
Search engines and print styles can use the structure

bank.q: Write the HTML for a student registration form with text, email, password, radio, checkbox, dropdown, textarea and a submit button. State exactly what the browser sends on submit.
outline: <form action="/register" method="post"> wrapper
Every control has a name; label with for/id pairs
Correct types: email, password, radio with same name, checkbox, select/option, textarea
Submit button type="submit"
Browser sends name=value pairs, url-encoded, in the request body because method is post
Unchecked boxes and unselected radios send nothing

bank.q: Write the HTML for a table showing three students and their marks in three subjects, using caption, thead, tbody and th scope. Show where colspan and rowspan are used.
outline: table > caption, thead > tr > th, tbody > tr > td
th scope="col" for column heads, scope="row" for row heads
colspan merges cells across a row; rowspan merges down a column
One row for the total using colspan=1 + td
Tables for data only, not for page layout

bank.q: Write CSS for a horizontal navigation bar and a product card with padding, border, border-radius and a subtle shadow. Explain each declaration you use.
outline: Remove list bullets and set display: flex on the ul for a horizontal bar
Anchor styling: display block, padding, colour, hover state
Card: width or max-width, padding, border, border-radius, box-shadow
background-color and color for contrast
Hover transition is optional but should be explained

bank.q: Use Flexbox and a media query to build a row of three cards that becomes a single stacked column on screens narrower than 600 px. Give the HTML and the CSS.
outline: Container: display: flex; gap; flex-wrap: wrap
Each card: flex: 1 1 30% or flex-basis
Media query @media (max-width: 600px) with flex-direction: column
Viewport meta tag in head for phones
justify-content and align-items explained

bank.q: Write a Bootstrap page with a navbar, a container, a row and three col-md-4 columns. Explain what each class does without writing new CSS.
outline: Include the Bootstrap CSS link in head
navbar, navbar-expand-lg, navbar-brand, nav-link
container centres and pads content
row creates the 12-column flex grid; col-md-4 takes 4 of 12 from the md breakpoint
Below md the columns stack; utility classes like mt-3 add spacing

bank.q: Write an HTML page that embeds a video with controls and fallback text, an audio clip, and an iframe showing a map. State the attributes that keep the media accessible.
outline: <video controls width="..."> with <source src type="video/mp4">
Fallback text between the tags for old browsers
<audio controls> with a source
<iframe src title width height loading="lazy">
title on iframe for screen readers; no autoplay for accessibility

bank.q: Compare Flexbox and CSS Grid, and justify which you would choose for a navigation bar, a page skeleton and a photo gallery.
outline: Flexbox = one dimension, content-driven sizing
Grid = two dimensions, layout-driven, rows and columns defined together
Nav bar: Flexbox, items in one row with gap
Page skeleton: Grid, named areas for header, main, aside, footer
Gallery: Grid with repeat(auto-fill, minmax(...))
Both can nest inside each other

bank.q: A form sends a password field with method GET. Analyse what the browser actually transmits, compare it with POST, and recommend the correct design including client-side and server-side validation.
outline: GET puts pairs in the URL query string: visible in history, logs, shoulder-surfing, length-limited
POST puts pairs in the body: not in the URL, still not encrypted without HTTPS
Passwords must use POST over HTTPS plus autocomplete and type=password
Client validation via required, type, pattern, minlength is convenience only
Server must re-validate; never trust the browser
Also mention that the URL is bookmarked and cached with GET

bank.q: Two rules target the same paragraph and conflict. Explain step by step how the browser picks the winner, compute specificity for given selectors, and evaluate whether a framework like Bootstrap is a better choice than hand-written CSS for a college project.
outline: Cascade order: origin and importance, then specificity, then source order
Specificity convention: inline 1000, id 100, class/attribute/pseudo-class 10, element/pseudo-element 1, added across the selector
Worked example: p.note (11) beats p (1); #main p (101) beats p.note
!important overrides normal author rules but breaks maintainability
Frameworks: faster, consistent, responsive out of the box; cost is page weight, look-alike sites, class-name learning
Verdict argued with the project's size, deadline and need for a custom design

glossary.def: HyperText Markup Language, the language that describes the structure and meaning of a web page with tags.
The line <!DOCTYPE html> at the top of a file that makes the browser use standards mode rather than quirks mode.

The angle-bracket marker such as

or

that opens or closes an element.
A start tag, its content and its end tag taken together as one node of the document tree.
A name=value pair inside a start tag that supplies extra information to the element.
An element that cannot hold content and therefore has no end tag, such as img or input.
Placing one element completely inside another, which creates the parent-child tree of the document.
An a element whose href gives the destination loaded when the user clicks the text or image.
An address written relative to the current page, such as images/logo.png, so the site can move as a folder.
An input, select, textarea or button element that collects one piece of user data.
The ?name=value&name=value part appended to a URL, used by forms with method="get".
The form attribute that sets how the body is encoded, for example multipart/form-data for file uploads.
Choosing tags for what the content means (nav, article, footer) rather than only for how it looks.
An inline frame element that embeds a complete separate document inside the current page.
A selector plus a declaration block, the basic unit of a stylesheet.
The pattern at the start of a CSS rule that decides which elements are styled, for example .card or li a.
A four-part weight (inline, id, class, element) that decides which of two conflicting rules wins.
The set of rules — origin, importance, specificity, source order — the browser uses to resolve conflicting declarations.
The arrangement of content, padding, border and margin that decides the size and spacing of every element.
The innermost part of an element's box, holding the text or child boxes, whose size is set by width and height.
An element with display: flex whose direct children are laid out as flex items along one main axis.
A layout with display: grid that places items in named or numbered rows and columns at the same time.
An @media condition that applies a block of CSS only when the screen matches, such as max-width: 768px.
The head element <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> that makes a phone report its real width.
The screen width at which a responsive layout switches to a different arrangement of columns.
A framework class that sets exactly one property, such as text-center or mt-3, used to avoid writing new CSS.
